Use case: precise-object-edit, game UI sprite material study.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the existing blue single release note sprite, a wide 5:1 rectangle. Image 2 is a STYLE AND COLOR REFERENCE ONLY: its matching long-note body.
Output ONLY one edited version of Image 1 as a flat, front-view sprite, tightly filling the entire 5:1 rectangular image canvas (e.g. 2000×400). Preserve its exact silhouette, proportions, angular panel boundaries, original palette family, symmetry and all unspecified artwork. No surrounding canvas, mockup, body attached, text, numbers, labels, multiple proposals, or cast shadow.
The user wants these specific local changes:
(5) The two horizontal white/neon stripes on the upper-middle left and right side panels are much too strong. Retain their narrow horizontal positions but substantially reduce luminosity and bloom; make them restrained colored highlights, not blown-out white luminous bars. Keep them clearly distinct from the adjacent faces.
(3) The bright U-shaped line that follows both sloping sides and the lower horizontal edge of the central face must become an ACTUALLY DARK recessed boundary, like the dark navy-blue channel around the beam in Image 2. Remove its neon glow and white core along the U. The existing small separate centered light spot at the bottom may remain; do not spread it along the U. Preserve line position and geometry.
(4) The upper side faces ABOVE the horizontal stripes should be cel shaded like the body reference: separate a few clean light, middle and shadow planes with deliberate angular transitions and restrained contrast. Do NOT just flood fill them with a single flat color. Do NOT use shiny metal smooth airbrush gradients or extra ornate bevels. Keep the current outer boundaries and use the body's stepped panel-shading vocabulary.
Keep the central face, one groups of three tight upward chevrons (top strong, middle 80%, bottom 50%), lower side faces, outer end strips and their layout recognizable and unchanged. The chevron group stays centered at 50% width.
Aim for a coherent release end to the referenced body: less aggressive lateral glow, dark U channel, crisp multi-tone cel-shaded upper faces, no extra 3D depth. Keep the asset overall bright and readable; only the requested U channel becomes dark.
